newsitem.title: TURKEY: Akin Tekstil raises H1 sales by 100 pct.
newsitem.headline: Akin Tekstil raises H1 sales by 100 pct.

text.p: Turkey's textile and ready to wear producer Akin Tekstil increased turnover by 100 percent in the first half of 1997 and boosted profitability, general manager Mehmet Cagis said on Tuesday.
The company aims to boost turnover to 11 trillion lira ($69 million) in 1997 from 5.7 trillion lira last year and to improve profitability again, he told Reuters.
"Our total sales increased by 100 percent in the first half of the year, despite the plunge of the German mark against the dollar,", Cagis said.
"Because we do all our sales in marks, after its plunge the mark could not rise enough against the lira to compensate for the Turkish inflation rate," he said.
Turkish inflation is currently around 78 percent.
Shares of the company opened at 10,750 lira on Tuesday, against 10,500 lira at Monday's close.
Cagis said the firm exported more than 50 percent of total production in the first half of 1997, adding: "This ratio increased to more than 60 percent in the last two months."
He said total exports calculated in dollars increased by 45 percent with yarn exports increasing by 57 percent in the first half of 1997 against the same period of 1996.
Akin Tekstil targets $38 to $40 million in exports in 1997.
The company increased its ready to wear products production by 49 percent in the first half.
Cagis said first-half profitability was above that of last year and added: "This better profitability is a result of last year's investments to overcome bottle-necks in the production lines."
Profitability would increase in the rest of the year because the group had begun to produce its own electricity from a natural-gas power plant last month, he said.
The company has built a new plant in Luleburgaz in western Turkey and began to move its yarn and texture painting facilities there.

Akin Tekstil reported 1.82 trillion lira in turnover in the first three months of 1997, against 1.09 trillion a year earlier. Net profit fell to 111 billion lira from 162 billion in the same period. ($1=159,100 lira)
